Pricing

How the charging works, what moves the price, and what you are told before anyone starts.

Ask for a price Call 07700 900707

Two ways work is priced

Most jobs fall into one of two shapes, and which one yours is decides how it is costed.

Charged by callout and labour

Repairs, diagnosis and most plumbing work. There is a callout or first-hour charge, then labour, then parts at cost plus any handling. You are told the price of the repair before a part goes in.

The first hour on site is £75, which covers attendance and diagnosis. There is no separate callout fee on top. Labour after the first hour is £55 an hour, charged in half-hour units.

Quoted as a fixed price

Boiler installations, bathroom work and anything that can be specified in advance. You get a written quotation covering the work, the materials and the time, and that is the price unless the job itself changes.

A written quotation holds for 30 days from the date we send it.

What moves the price

  • Access — a boiler in a loft or a pipe under a floor takes longer than one on a wall
  • Parts availability — an obsolete part may have to be sourced rather than carried
  • Whether the existing system needs work to take a new appliance
  • When you need it — out-of-hours and emergency attendance are charged differently

Outside our normal hours, and for emergency attendance, the first hour is £120, with labour at £80 an hour after that.

What you are told, and when

The principle is simple: nothing is charged that you have not agreed to first.

  1. Before the visit, you are told the callout or first-hour charge, or given a quotation if the job can be specified in advance.
  2. On site, once the fault is identified, you get a price for the repair before any part is fitted.
  3. If the job turns out to be bigger than it looked, work stops and you are told what changed and what it costs before anything further happens.
  4. The invoice itemises labour, parts and anything else separately.

Surveys and quotations

A boiler installation needs someone to look at the property before a real price can be given — the flue route, the gas supply, the radiators and the water pressure all affect it. Survey visits for installation quotations are free, and there is no obligation to go ahead.

See boiler installation for what the survey covers.

Payment and VAT

We take bank transfer, debit and credit cards. Payment is due within 14 days of the invoice.

All prices on this site include VAT at the standard rate. Our VAT number is GB 123 4567 89.

Certain energy-saving and heating work qualifies for a reduced rate of VAT in some circumstances. Whether that applies depends on the work and on your situation, so it is worth asking rather than assuming either way.

Service plans

Our annual cover plan is £18 a month and includes the yearly service, priority booking, and parts and labour on covered repairs.

Common questions

Will I be told the price before work starts?

Yes. For a repair you get a price for the repair before any part is fitted. For an installation you get a written quotation before anything is ordered. Nothing is charged beyond what you have agreed without being asked first.

What happens if the job turns out to be bigger than expected?

Work stops and you are told what has been found, what it changes and what it costs, before anything further is done. A revised price is something you agree to, not something that appears on the invoice afterwards.

Do you charge for a quotation?

Survey visits for installation quotations are free, and there is no obligation to go ahead.

Is there a minimum charge?

The minimum charge is one hour, £75, even where the work itself takes less time.

How do I pay?

We take bank transfer, debit and credit cards. Payment is due within 14 days of the invoice.

Is the work guaranteed?

Our workmanship is guaranteed for 12 months. Parts carry whatever warranty the manufacturer provides, which we pass on to you in full.
